Так [сказано] там же:
Чета ловок в устроении [встреч], тайный в делах, смел умом;
здесь, в Гокуле, это, как сказано, Бхангура, Бхрингара и другие.*
notes: В бенгальском двустишии 3637 — Бхринга, в шлоке — Бхрингара.

verses.text:
Здесь же друзья-виты — Кадара, Бхарати и другие,
искусные в убранстве Кришны: дивен [их] обычай.*
notes: В шлоке 3640 — Бхаратибандха.

verses.text:
Там же:
Искусный в нарядах и украшениях, хитрый, сведущий в собраниях,
знающий искусства науки любви — зовётся витой;
Кадара, Бхаратибандха и прочие названы витами.

Здесь друзья-видушаки — Васанта и другие —
умножают веселье, когда Кришна ест.

Там же:
Именуемый Васантой и прочими, жадный до еды, любящий ссоры,
смешащий [всех] нелепыми телодвижениями, речами и нарядом, — [таков] видушака;
как этот Мадхумангала, прославленный в «Видагдха-мадхаве».

Питхамарда Шридама — нет предела его достоинствам;
как много он здесь помогает Кришне!

Там же:
Кто достоинствами подобен герою (наяке) и с любовью следует за ним, —
тот зовётся питхамардой; таков у Хари Шридама.

Здесь прия-нарма-сакхи — Субала и другие:
что приносит Кришне счастье, то они и делают всеми способами.

Там же:
Знающий самые сокровенные тайны, принявший настроение сакхи,
он — лучший из всех любящих друзей, прия-нарма-сакха;
в Гокуле же это Субала, а также Арджуна и другие.*
notes: Арджуна — пастушок, задушевный друг Кришны во Врадже (не сын Панду).

verses.text:
О Шриниваса! В этой прелестной роще Кришна
Сам встречается [с гопи]: звуком флейты Он влечёт гопи.

Как у Радхики есть сваям-дути и апта-дути,
так и у Шри Кришны: в этом — безмерное блаженство.*
notes: Сваям-дути — «сама [себе] посланница»: влюблённый, который сам открывает свою любовь; апта-дути — «доверенная посланница» (см. 3649–3653, 3670–3673).

verses.text:
Там же:
Те посланницы, о которых будет сказано в разделе о возлюбленных Хари, —
их и здесь знатокам расы следует понимать соответственно.
Там — сваям (Сам) и вамши (флейта). («Сваям» — то есть сваям-дути.)

Вира, Вринда и другие — апта-дути Шри Кришны;
в этой кундже они сводят [Их] обоих — какой дивный способ!

Там же:
Вира, Вринда и другие прославлены также как доверенные посланницы Кришны:
Вира дерзка на речи, Вринда искусна в льстивых словах.

Вира и прочие названы особыми посланницами Хари;
а те, о которых будет сказано, кончая Лингини, — общие для обоих.*
notes: Перевод — по изд. 1960 г. «অস্যাসাধারণা» (asyāsādhāraṇāḥ, «Его особые»); в A по скану — «অন্যাঃ সাধারণা দূত্যো» («другие — общие посланницы»), в C — «অস্যাঃ সাধারণা»; принято чтение изд. 1960 г., согласное со второй строкой (там «общие для обоих» противопоставлены особым). Лингини — странствующая подвижница, одна из посланниц в «Удджвала-ниламани».

verses.text:
Что сказать о том, как здесь сакхи и прочие [подруги] Радхики
помогают [Ей], — этого не изложить подробно.

Сакхи Радхики — пяти видов: сакхи, а также
нитья-сакхи, прана-сакхи и прочие — так [о них] известно.

Взяв всех этих сакхи, прекрасная Радхика
пребывает в этой кундже, глядя на путь Кришны.

Там же:
Сакхи же Владычицы Вриндавана, как считается, пяти видов:
сакхи, и нитья-сакхи, и некие прана-сакхи,
и прия-сакхи, и прославленные парама-прештха-сакхи.

Сакхи Кусумика, Виндхья, Дхаништха и другие здесь
усердно исполняют то, что у Радхики на сердце.

Там же:
Сакхи — [это] прославленные Кусумика, Виндхья, Дхаништха и другие.

Нитья-сакхи — Кастури, Маниманджарика и другие —
здесь неустанно исполняют желания Радхи.

Там же:
Нитья-сакхи же — Кастури, Маниманджарика и другие.

Прана-сакхи — Васанти и другие — почти равны Радхе;
в этой кундже они умножают веселье Радхи и Кришны.

Там же:
Прана-сакхи — Шашимукхи, Васанти, Ласика и другие;
они по большей части обрели сходство (сварупату) с Владычицей Вриндавана.
(«Сварупата» — то есть равенство.)*
notes: Глосса — по изд. 1912/13 г. (B); в изд. 1960 г. её нет.

verses.text:
Прия-сакхи — Курангакши и другие, несравненные, —
в этой кундже, видя красоту [Их] обоих, вне себя [от восторга].

Там же:
Прия-сакхи — Курангакши, Сумадхья, Маданаласа,
Камала, Мадхури, Манджукеши, Кандарпа-сундари,
Мадхави, Малати, Камалата, Шашикала и другие.

Парама-прештха-сакхи — Лалита и другие — здесь,
сведя [Их] обоих, полны великой радости в сердце.

Там же:
Парама-прештха-сакхи же — Лалита вместе с Вишакхикой,
Сучитра, Чампакалата, Тунгавидья, Индулекхика,

Рангадеви и Судеви — эти восемь первые из всех групп;*
из них лишь у двух по высшему пределу премы
кое-где порой, кое-где порой как бы видится превосходство.
notes: «সর্বগণাগ্রিমাঃ» по A (сверено по скану)/B — «первые из всех групп»; в C и изд. 1960 г. — «সর্বগুণাগ্রিমাঃ», «первые по всем достоинствам».

verses.text:
О Шриниваса! В этой обители-никундже
сваям-дути и апта-дути являют [свою] ловкость.

Так [сказано] там же:
Теперь о них, прибегающих к помощницам из жажды встречи с Кришной, —
описывается, как [они] пользуются посланницами в пурва-раге и прочем;
посланница здесь названа двоякой: сама (сваям) и доверенная (апта).

Сваям-дути здесь, увидев Кришну,
достигает цели — словом, телом и взглядом.

Сваям-дути Шри Радхика во всём искусна;
[Она] предаётся играм в этой кундже — счастью нет предела.

Там же:
Та, чья стыдливость рушится от чрезмерного нетерпения и которая, очарованная рагой и прочим,
сама изъявляет [любовь], — потому и зовётся сваям-дути.
Собственные изъявления, как сказано, трёх видов: словесные, телесные и зрительные.

О Шриниваса! В этой роще кадамб
апта-дути всегда желают Радхе счастья.

Деяния доверенных посланниц не пересказать;
их три [вида]: амитартха, нисриштартха, патрахари.*
notes: Виды доверенных посланниц (апта-дути) по «Удджвала-ниламани»: амитартха — сама угадывающая по намёкам [чувства обоих], нисриштартха — которой поручено дело, патрахари — носящая письма (3677–3682).

verses.text:
Там же:
Та, что не нарушит доверия даже ценой жизни,
ласковая и красноречивая, — она посланница прекраснобровых гопи;
она трёх видов: амитартха, нисриштартха и патрахари.
(Вишрамбха — то есть доверие.)

Посланница-амитартха, весьма искусная в [понимании] намёков,
придумав средство, соединяет здесь обоих.

Там же:
Та, что, узнав по знакам чувство обоих или одного из двоих,
соединит их двоих [разными] средствами, — она будет амитартха.

Посланнице-нисриштартхе вверяют бремя дела;
в этой кундже она хитроумием устраивает встречу двоих.

Там же:
Та, кому один из двоих вверил бремя дела
и кто хитроумием соединит обоих, — она зовётся нисриштартха.

Посланница-патрахари лишь, взяв письмо,
передаёт [его] обоим, и двое встречаются, придя в никунджу.

Там же:
Та, что лишь передаёт весточки юной чете, — патрахарика.

Посланницы — мастерица, прорицательница, отшельница, а также
служанка, молочная сестра — повсюду известны;*
notes: Мастерица (шилпакари), прорицательница (дайваджня), отшельница (лингини), служанка (паричарика), молочная сестра (дхатрейи — дочь кормилицы), лесные богини (вана-деви), сакхи — виды посланниц в «Удджвала-ниламани» (3685).

verses.text:
лесные богини, сакхи и другие — все они в этих кунджах
с радостным сердцем являют каждая свои достоинства.

Так [сказано] там же:
Они — мастерица, прорицательница, отшельница, служанка,
молочная сестра, лесная богиня, сакхи и прочие — во Врадже.

Мастерица, сведущая здесь во многих ремёслах,
показывая [своё] мастерство, радует обоих.

Доверенная посланница-прорицательница, искусная в исчислениях,
предсказывает сегодняшнюю встречу двоих в этой кундже.*
notes: «Сегодняшнюю» — по A (по скану: «কহে এই কুঞ্জে অদ্য দোঁহার ঘটনা») и B (অদ্য, adya); в изд. 1960 г. «অন্য» (anya, «другой»).

verses.text:
Отшельница — в одеянии подвижницы, как Паурнамаси;
Паурнамаси, придя сюда, соединяет обоих.

Там же:
Отшельница — в одеянии подвижницы, как, сказано, Паурнамаси.

Служанки — Лаванга-манджари и другие — с радостью
соединяют Радхику с Кришной в этой кундже.*
notes: Лаванга-манджари и Бханумати — служанки (паричарики) Радхи.

verses.text:
Там же:
Лаванга-манджари, Бханумати и прочие — служанки.

Молочная сестра, приведя Радху из Джавата,
весело соединяет Её с Кришной в этой кундже.

Лесные богини всё время пребывают в лесу;
в этой кундже они видят встречу Раи и Кану.

Сакхи весело соединяет обоих в этой кундже;
обычай сакхи известен — кто не поёт [ей] славу?

Там же:
Та, что бесхитростно питает взаимную прему, бо́льшую даже, чем к самой себе,
доверчивая, равная по возрасту, одежде и прочему, — считается сакхи.

Её служение посланницы для обоих — двоякое: явное и подразумеваемое.
(Тат — то есть этой сакхи; убхайох — то есть героя и героини.)

Разными способами в этой обители-никундже
сакхи умножает счастье двоих в самбхоге.*
notes: Самбхога — наслаждение соединения возлюбленных, в противоположность випраламбхе (разлуке). Главная (мукхья) самбхога — наяву, второстепенная (гауна) — во сне; у каждой по четыре вида (3698–3701).

verses.text:
Как главная и второстепенная, самбхога — восьми видов:
после пурва-раги и прочего — санкшипта и прочие, так изложено.

Так [сказано] там же:
Чувство, что через благоприятное вкушение взглядов, объятий и прочего
восходит к ликованию юной четы, именуется самбхогой.

Мудрые объявляют её двоякой: главной и второстепенной.
Главная самбхога — в состоянии бодрствования; она — четырёх видов.

Возникающие по порядку после пурва-раги, после маны и после двух [видов] правасы,
их знают как санкшипту, санкирну, сампанну и самриддхиман.*
notes: Праваса — разлука из-за отъезда возлюбленного, недалёкого или далёкого. Санкшипта — «краткая», санкирна — «смешанная», сампанна — «обретённая», самриддхиман — «преисполненная» самбхога (3702–3712).

verses.text:
В пурва-раге — санкшипта-самбхога: кратко
сакхи соединяет здесь обоих своим способом.

Там же:
Где юная чета из робости, стыдливости и прочего
вкушает сдержанные ласки, — та [самбхога] названа санкшиптой.

Когда разными способами мана преодолена,
здесь, в санкирна-самбхоге, сакхи обретает счастье.

Там же:
Где ласки смешиваются с воспоминанием об обидах и прочим,
та [самбхога] — санкирна, приятная, как слегка подогретый сахарный тростник.

После недалёкой правасы — сампанна; у неё два вида;
здесь сакхи вкушает счастье самбхоги.

Там же:
Наслаждение, когда возлюбленный соединился [с ней] после правасы, названо сампанной;
эта встреча двояка: агати и прадурбхава.

Агати:
Приход, [совершаемый] по обычаю мирского поведения, — агати.

Прадурбхава:
Когда перед дорогими [Ему], охваченными волнением премы, Хари
внезапно является, — это называется прадурбхавой.

Самриддхиман-самбхога — после далёкой правасы;
по различию тайного и явного она разыгрывается в этой кундже.

Там же:
Избыток наслаждения юной четы, разлучённой из-за зависимости [от других],
которой трудно увидеть друг друга, — зовётся самриддхиман.

Там же:
Иные признают у них двоякий вид — по различию тайного и явного;
хотя это и принято, здесь [о нём] не сказано, ибо оно не приносит большого ликования.

О Шриниваса, этой тропой Раи с радостью
входит в этот дом-кунджу вместе с подругами.

Сколько ни есть подруг у Радхики — им нет конца;
среди сакхи во главе с Лалитой — дивная красота.

Сакхи Шри Лалита, во всех достоинствах совершенная,
окружена восьмёркой [подруг] — Ратнапрабхой и другими.*
notes: Во всех копиях «অষ্টগুণে» («восемью качествами»); по смыслу и по 3717–3729 — «অষ্টগণে» («восьмёркой подруг»).

verses.text:
Так [сказано] в «Шри Брихат-кришна-ганоддеша-дипике»:
Ратнапрабха, Ратикала, Субхадра, Бхадрарекхика,
Сумукхи, и Дхаништха, и Калахамси, Калапини.*
notes: Название — по A/B («শ্রীবৃহৎকৃষ্ণগণোদ্দেশদীপিকায়াং»), в изд. 1960 г. искажено; по-видимому, большая редакция «Радха-кришна-ганоддеша-дипики» Рупы Госвами. В 3716–3730 — восьмёрки подруг при каждой из восьми главных сакхи Радхи.

verses.text:
Красоте Вишакхи нет сравнения;
окружённая восьмёркой [подруг] — Мадхави и другими, — она сияет.

Так [сказано] там же:
Малати, Мадхави, Чандрарекхика, а также Кунджари,
Харини, [та, что] по имени Чапала, Сурабхи и Шубханана.*
notes: Порядок «Малати, Мадхави» — по A/B/C; в изд. 1960 г. первой названа Мадхави, как в 3717.

verses.text:
Во всём искусная, прекрасного нрава Сучитра*
окружена своей восьмёркой — Курангакши и другими.
notes: Во всех копиях «সুচিত্রাদি» (suchitrādi, «Сучитра и прочие»); переведено по смыслу.

verses.text:
Там же:
Курангакши, Сучарита, Мандали, Маникундала,
Чандрика, Чандралатика, Кундакакши, Сумандира.

Сладость Чампакалаты чудесна безмерно;
с восьмёркой [подруг] — Расаликой и другими — дивная красота.

Там же:
Расалика, Тилакини, Шаурасени, Сугандхика,
Камини, Каманагари, Нагари, Нагавеника.*
notes: Камини — по A (по скану: «কামিনী কামনগরী») и B; в изд. 1960 г. «রামিনী» (Рамини), в C «বামিনী» (Вамини).

verses.text:
Кто сохранит самообладание при [виде] красоты Шри Рангадеви?
Красота её восьмёрки — Манджумедхи и других — похищает сердце.

Там же:
Манджумедха, Сумадхура, Сумадхья, Мадхурекшана,
Танумадхья, Мадхусандра, Гуначуда, Варангада.

Судеви всегда цветёт от любви к Радхике;
её восьмёрка — Тунгабхадра и другие — известна.

Там же:
Тунгабхадра, Расоттунга, Рангавати, Сусангата,
Читралекха, Вичитранги, Медини, Маданаласа.*
notes: Рангавати — по A (по скану: «রঙ্গবাটী সুসঙ্গতা»), B и C; в изд. 1960 г. «রঙ্গবাটা» (Рангавата).

verses.text:
Тунгавидья — высшая красавица, красота её велика;
её восьмёрка — Калакантхи и другие — дивного нрава.

Там же:
Калакантхи, Шашикала, Камала, Мадхура, Индира,
Кандарпасундари, Камалатика, Премаманджари.*
notes: «মধুরেন্দিরা» понято как два имени — Мадхура и Индира, — иначе в перечне семь имён.

verses.text:
Индулекха — прекрасного нрава, притягивает все сердца;
с чем сравнить её восьмёрку — Кавери и других?

Там же:
Кавери, Чарукавара, Сукеши, Манджукешика,
Харахира, Махахира, Харакантхи, Манохара.

О Шриниваса, вместе с подругами Лалиты и других
в этой кундже, с радостью видя встречу двоих,

каждый миг [они] не могут сдержать сердца от ликования, —
[таковы] дивные деяния сакхи — Лалиты и других.

Так [сказано] в «Шри Удджвала-ниламани»:
Взаимное прославление любви (1) и достоинств (2) [обоих], пробуждение в них привязанности (3),
[устройство] абхисары (4) для них обоих, предоставление сакхи Кришне (5),
шутки (6), утешение (7), наряжание (8), умение раскрывать [чувства] сердца (9),
сокрытие её недостатков (10), обман мужа и прочих (11),*
notes: «Удджвала-ниламани», раздел о сакхи: семнадцать действий сакхи. Номера (1)–(17) стоят в тексте изд. 1888 и 1912/13 гг.; в изд. 1960 г. их нет.

verses.text:
наставление (12), соединение [их] в должное время (13), служение с опахалом и прочим (14),
упрёки им обоим (15), а также пересылка весточек (16),
старания и прочее для сбережения жизни героини (17) — [таковы] действия сакхи.
О Шриниваса, это не описать словами:

verses_en.text:
O Srinivasa, Krishna is the embodiment of rasa;
what power have I to tell which lilas [He performed] in which places?

In all the varieties of nayaka He sports;
the crown of nayakas is the son of the king of Vraja.

Thus [it is said] in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu:
The crest-jewel of nayakas is Krishna, the Supreme Lord Himself.

By the distinction of abodes the kinds of nayaka are ninety-six, 96;
in Vraja Krishna is purnatama, [His] bhava is upapati.*
notes: The ninety-six kinds of nayaka (hero) according to the Ujjvala-nilamani: four by temperament (dhirodatta, dhiralalita, dhirashanta, dhiroddhata; see 3484–3495), two by status (pati, the husband; upapati, a lover who is not the husband), four by relation to the heroines (anukula, dakshina, shatha, dhrishta), and three by fullness — purna, purnatara, purnatama (in Dvaraka, Mathura and Vraja).

verses_en.text:
With thousands upon thousands of yutheshvaris
He playfully displays the acts of all [kinds of] nayaka.*
notes: Yutheshvaris are the leaders of the groups (yuthas) of gopis.

verses_en.text:
Among the yuthas the most excellent are Chandravali and Sri Radhika;
everywhere it is known that of them Radhika is the higher.

Thus [it is said] in the Ujjvala-nilamani:
But even among them, in every way the most excellent are the two — Radha and Chandravali,
whose yuthas [number] millions of doe-eyed ones.

The rasa was crowded with hundreds of millions of young maidens
on that bank of the Yamuna — such is the tradition of the agamas.

But even of these two Radhika is higher in every way:
She is the embodiment of mahabhava; She far surpasses [all] in qualities.

What Krishna's pastimes with Sri Radhika are like —
who has the power to describe that in detail?

Here Krishna sports in the greatest merriment,
displaying the acts of a dhirodatta nayaka.

The dhirodatta is highly skilled in every respect,
supremely grave, [his] ways pure — humility and the rest.

Thus [it is said] in the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu:
Grave, humble, forbearing, compassionate, firm in his vows,
not boastful, with hidden pride, magnanimous — [such is] the dhirodatta.
This one is like Raghunatha.*
notes: Examples for the definitions of the four kinds of hero: Raghunatha (Rama) is dhirodatta, Kandarpa dhiralalita (3489), Yudhishthira dhirashanta (3492), Bhimasena dhiroddhata (3495). The 1960 edition lacks the lines with Raghunatha and Bhimasena.

verses_en.text:
Krishna, the charming dhiralalita nayaka,
sports unceasingly in this kunja temple.

Clever, carefree, very fond of jesting,
subject to His beloved, [His] ways are supreme bliss.

There:
Clever, in fresh youth, a master of jests,
carefree — [such is] the dhiralalita; he is mostly subject to his beloved.
This one is like Kandarpa.

The dhirashanta nayaka is Sri, the son of the king of Vraja,
a knower of the shastras, master of His senses, supremely righteous.

He displays humility and other virtues at His beloved's side;
in this kunja house there are wonderfully marvellous pastimes.

There:
Even-tempered, enduring hardship, discerning,
endowed with humility and other virtues — [such a one] is called dhirashanta.
This one is like Yudhishthira.

Whatever the virtues and acts of a dhiroddhata nayaka are,
Krishna displays [them] here so that His beloved rejoices.

Self-praise and the rest in Him are the greatest wonder;
the merriment that [was] in this kunja cannot be described in full.

There:
Jealous, proud, wily, wrathful, fickle
and boastful — [such a one] the wise have called dhiroddhata.
This one is like Bhimasena.

O Srinivasa, Krishna, the embodiment of rasa,
revealed the ways of an anukula nayaka.

There is no equal to the anukula nayaka:
anukula is attachment to one nayika.

The anukula nayaka is Sri, the prince of Vraja;
here are [His] wonderful pastimes with Rai alone.

Thus [it is said] in the Ujjvala-nilamani:
He who, through excessive attachment to [one] woman, has given up longing for other beauties,
like Rama toward Sita — he is called anukula.

Toward Radha alone is Krishna's famed devotion (anukulata):
at the sight of Her He never recalls association with others.

How Krishna is subject to Radha's prema, what the love of the two of Them is —
that way the poets describe in various manners.

Thus [it is said] in the Gaura-charitra-chintamani — Sri Yamuna speaks to Ganga — in a song (raga Pauravi):*
O you, dear [to me] as life, friend full of joy!
I am sold to your virtues.
Now I shall tell — listen: [of her]
with whom Shyamasundara's love is greater.
notes: The Gaura-charitra-chintamani is a Bengali work by Narahari Chakravarti himself. The songs 3502–3515 are the words of the Yamuna to the Ganga: the dark Yamuna and the white Ganga, as friends, speak of the love of dark Krishna and golden Radha.

verses_en.text:
Chandravali in Vraja is a renowned beauty;
before [her] wondrous beauty Rama is ashamed;
a young beauty full of rasa —
in virtues and character she has no equal.

In a fine new nikunja temple
she sports merrily with Shyama every day;
Shyama, full of rasa, is likewise enraptured —
who can grasp the way of [His] subjection to her prema?

When [He] floats in the ocean of supreme bliss,
touching that jewel of a beauty,
immersed in drinking the nectar of [her] moon-face —
then nothing [else] comes to the nagara's mind.

If at that time the fragrance of Radha's body,
reaching [Him], touches [His] nostrils ever so slightly —
at once, leaving her, the restless
Dark One runs as if gone mad.

What more shall I say? Know in your heart
with whom Kanu's love is greater.
Narahari offers himself for such prema —
who can find the bottom in counting [Her] virtues?

Again there (raga Kamoda):
What shall I say, O [friend]: incomparable in the world
is the love of Radha and Madhava.
The life is one, but the bodies separate: who
fashioned [Them so], with what joy?

If you say, "Since the two are one, why then
did the colour of the two become different?" —
of that I shall tell you a little;
listen to it with care.

There are many colours; among them is shyama,
[but] in the gaura colour there is greater beauty.
Showing its utmost to the world,
[it] shines, alluring the eyes of the people of the world.*
notes: Shyama is the dark colour of Krishna, gaura the golden colour of Radha. The understanding of the second half of the stanza is conjectural: তাহার অবধি দেখায়া জগতে, হাসে জগজন নয়নলোভা (tāhāra avadhi dekhāyā jagate, hāse jagajana nayana-lobhā).

verses_en.text:
And I say more: O [friend], the restless Dark One,
when He sees playful Radha,
eagerly longing, spreads out both arms
and yearns to take [Her] in His embrace.

If at that time people of the rivals' party
suddenly see this nearby,
some, deceived by the semblance of a cloud with lightning,
cannot make out this great play.*
notes: Dark Krishna in golden Radha's embrace resembles a thundercloud with lightning.

verses_en.text:
And I say more: that skilful poet, the Creator,
to give great joy to many people,
gazing on the loveliness of shyama and gaura,
[resolved,] "I shall compose comparisons in many ways."

That is why [They are] so [different] — [yet] not different at all:
Shyama's body is fashioned of Rai's prema.
The bodies of Radha and Kanu are full of prema —
the love of these bodies is known in the world.

The ways of these two — what will others know?
Only the rasikas know.
Whoever is deprived of this rasa,
Narahari counts him equal to a beast.

O Srinivasa, one day here
a meeting with Chandravali was arranged.

Krishna became eager to meet her;
she set out for the tryst with her own sakhis.

At that time, hearing that Radhika was going to the nikunja,
the son of the king of Vraja sets out from here.

Coming near Radhika, [He] lost His composure
and forgot everything — the meeting with Chandravali and the rest.

What pastimes there were in this kunja with Rai —
that I do not know how to tell, O Srinivasa.

Krishna is the dakshina-nayaka, His actions full of rasa;
one who is the same toward all nayikas is called dakshina.*
notes: Dakshina ("courteous"), shatha ("deceitful", 3533) and dhrishta ("brazen", 3535) are types of the hero-lover (nayaka) in his relation to his beloveds in Rupa Gosvami's Ujjvala-nilamani, along with anukula ("devoted to one", 3525).

verses_en.text:
How Krishnachandra sports here with His beloveds —
who could tell it?

There:
One who, even with his heart given to another, does not abandon respect, fear, love and courtesy toward his former beloved —
he should be known as dakshina.*
notes: The verses of this portion are from the Ujjvala-nilamani (the chapters on heroes and heroines); "there" refers to that book, cited above, although songs are quoted immediately before 3521.

verses_en.text:
Or:
Also one who is the same toward many nayikas is called dakshina.

The way that belongs to the nayaka who is dakshina and anukula
Krishna, the embodiment of rasa, displayed in the rasa [dance].

Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, in the Madhya-khanda, in the eighth chapter:
"The sacred rasa pastimes with a hundred crores of gopis;
among them, in one form He remains at Radha's side.*
notes: CC Madhya 8; the quotation runs 3526–3532. A crore is ten million.

verses_en.text:
Seeing ordinary love — equality everywhere —
Radha's crooked love turned into contrariness.

Angered, She left the rasa [dance] in pique and went away;
not seeing Her, Hari was distraught.

Krishna's whole desire, His wish, is the rasa-lila;
in the desire for the rasa-lila Radhika is the [binding] chain.

Without Her the rasa-lila does not please [His] heart;
leaving the circle, He went to search for Radha.

Wandering here and there and finding Radha nowhere,
He grieves, wearied by the arrows of Kama.

With a hundred crores of gopis [His] desire is not quenched —
from this I infer the virtues of Sri Radhika."

Here Krishna displays [the nature] of the shatha-nayaka:
to the face — pleasing; behind the back He acts unpleasingly.

Thus [it is said] in the Ujjvala-nilamani:
One who speaks pleasingly to her face, but elsewhere does much that is unpleasing
and [commits] a hidden offense — him the wise call shatha.

Here Krishna displays the actions of the dhrishta-nayaka
before the nayika, rejoicing.

Even with the marks of enjoyment with another nayika He is fearless,
exceedingly skilled in the use of false words.

There:
One who is fearless though the marks of enjoyment with another young [woman] are plain on him,
and skilled in false speech — he indeed is called dhrishta.

Here Krishna, with Radha, the beloved dear [to Him] as life,
[enjoys] pastimes in which He is beside Himself — who can describe them?

Radha, who is in the middle stage [of youth], is a mine of jewel-like virtues;
She is known as the crown of all nayikas.

As in Krishna the states of all nayakas are possible,
so in Sri Radhika are the states of all nayikas.

There:
As all the states of the nayaka without exception [belong] to Madhava,
so the states of the nayika, it is held, [belong] for the most part to Radha.

By distinction of place svakiya and parakiya are determined;
the varieties of nayika are three hundred and sixty.*
notes: Svakiya is "one's own" (married to the hero), parakiya is "another's" (bound to the hero by secret love); the text has স্বীয়া (svīyā), the same as svakiya. The Ujjvala-nilamani counts three hundred and sixty varieties of heroine.

verses_en.text:
In Vraja Radha is the parakiya, the highest nayika;
in the varieties — mugdha and the rest — She sports without limit.*
notes: Mugdha ("young, inexperienced"), madhya ("middle") and pragalbha ("mature, bold", 3562) are the three varieties of heroine (nayika) by youth and experience.

verses_en.text:
O Srinivasa, in this nikunja house
Krishna sports with the mugdha-nayika.

The mugdha is under the sway of the sakhi, her youth fresh;
in the skill of the new arts of love she is little practised.

In mana she is gentle, incapable [of it];
having united her with Krishna, the sakhi attains great happiness.

There:
The mugdha has new youth and [new] desire, is contrary in union, under the sway of the sakhi,
exceedingly bashful in love's acts, [yet making] charming hidden efforts;

when the beloved has offended, her gaze is choked with tears;
she is unable to speak either pleasing or unpleasing words, and in mana she always turns away.

She who turns away in mana is thus:
gentle, and also incapable [of mana] — so she who turns away in mana is of two kinds.*
notes: A (by the scan) reads «মৃদ্বী ১ তথা ক্ষমা ২», written separately, which also allows the reading kṣamā ("patient"); the translation follows 3546 («মৃদু অক্ষমা», "gentle, incapable").

verses_en.text:
Look at this nikunja, O Srinivasa:
here are Krishna's pastimes with the madhya beloved.

The madhya has manifest youth and is experienced in every way;
in mana she has three varieties: dhira and the rest.*
notes: Dhira ("composed"), adhira ("uncomposed") and dhira-adhira ("composed and uncomposed") are varieties of the madhya and the pragalbha by their conduct in mana (3554–3559, 3565–3570).

verses_en.text:
There:
[The madhya] has bashfulness and love's desire in equal measure, possesses blossoming youth,
is somewhat bold in speech, capable of union up to swooning;

the madhya is in mana now soft, now harsh;
in her conduct in mana she is threefold: dhira, adhira, and [combining] both.

The dhira-madhya, [being] in mana, here, in the precincts of this kunja,
addresses to Krishna barbed words [and] pure reproach.*
notes: "Pure reproach" — পবিত্র ভর্ৎসন (pavitra bhartsana) in all copies; apparently a reproach without coarse words, unlike the adhira (3556).

verses_en.text:
There:
The dhira, however, speaks to the offending beloved with barbed words, mockingly.

In this kunja the adhira-madhya, angry with the Lord of her life,
[speaks] fearless, cruel words that please the sakhis.

There:
The adhira in anger repulses the beloved with cruel words.

The dhira-adhira-madhya here, with tears,
speaks barbed words to Krishna, glancing at the sakhis.

There:
The dhira-adhira, however, speaks to the beloved with barbed words, with tears.

The madhya-nayika is the summit of all rasas;
the madhya Radha here bestows bliss on Krishna.

There:
All the excellence of rasa befits the madhya alone,
for in her innocence and boldness are plainly joined.

In this kunja the pragalbha, a beauty in the full bloom of youth,
displays so many artful ways to give Krishna happiness!

How eager she is for union cannot be told;
in her conduct in mana the pragalbha has three varieties: dhira and the rest.

There:
The pragalbha is in the full bloom of youth, blinded by intoxication, eager for abundant union,
versed in manifesting many bhavas, having overpowered her beloved with rasa;
her words and acts are very bold, and in mana she is extremely harsh.

In this kunja the dhira-pragalbha, skilled in mana,
concealing her anger, is indifferent to union.

There:
The dhira is indifferent in union, conceals [her feelings] and [remains] respectful.

The adhira-pragalbha in this nikunja house
strikes Krishna with the lotus [adorning her] ear, with cruel threats.

There:
The adhira, having threatened cruelly in anger, strikes the beloved.

The anger of the dhira-adhira-pragalbha is not noticeable;
in this kunja she threatens Krishna a little, with hints.*
notes: "With hints" follows the 1912/13 and 1888 editions (ভঙ্গিতে); the 1960 edition has ভর্ৎসিতে, "rebuking".

verses_en.text:
There:
She who has the qualities of the dhira and the adhira is called dhira-adhira.

See, Srinivasa: in this kunja Sri Radhika,
filled with prema, moves Krishna to abhisara.

Sri Radhika, making abhisara in secret,
in attire suited to the time, meets Krishna.

The abhisarika-nayika Radhika, the beauty,
comes and meets [Him], now with the sakhis, now alone.*
notes: Abhisarika ("she who goes to the tryst", 3571–3575), vasaka-sajja ("she who has made [the chamber] ready for the tryst", 3576–3580), virahotkanthita ("she who longs in separation", 3581–3585), khandita ("the wounded one", 3586–3588), vipralabdha ("the deceived one", 3589–3591), kalahantarita ("she who is parted by a quarrel", 3592–3594) and proshita-bhartrika ("she whose beloved is abroad", 3595–3596) are states of the heroine in the Ujjvala-nilamani; the eighth is svadhina-bhartrika ("she who rules her beloved").

verses_en.text:
There:
She who calls her beloved to a tryst and also goes [to him] herself —
she is the abhisarika; in attire fit for the way she [is] jyotsni or tamasi.*
notes: Jyotsni — [going to the tryst] on a moonlit night, tamasi — on a dark night; the attire accordingly light or dark.

verses_en.text:
As if hiding within her own body out of bashfulness, with all her ornaments [hushed] to silence,
veiled, with one loving sakhi, let her go to her beloved.

The vasaka-sajja-nayika in this kunja house
joyfully, with the sakhi, prepares the bed and the rest.

On the path by which Krishna will come she fixes her eyes,
again and again she looks out for the messenger.

The vasaka-sajja-nayika Radhika, the beauty —
what actions She displays I cannot tell.

There:
She who, when her beloved is to come at her turn (vasaka), adorns her body
and [makes ready] the chamber — she is the vasaka-sajjika.*
notes: Vasaka — the turn, the appointed day (night) of the tryst; vasaka-sajjika is the same as vasaka-sajja (3576).

verses_en.text:
Her actions are planning love's play, watching the path,
merry talk with the sakhi, looking again and again for the messenger, and the like.

In this kunja a meeting had been agreed upon;
because of Krishna's delay that eagerness faded.

Separation grew, the longing had no limit —
Radhika here is in the state of virahotkanthita.

She wonders why Krishna has not come;
[Her] actions — burning of the heart, trembling and the rest — cannot be told.

There:
She who longs when her blameless dearest one delays —
[her] the knowers of feelings call virahotkanthita.

Her actions are burning of the heart, trembling, guessing at the cause,
joylessness, shedding of tears, telling of her own state, and the like.

Bearing on Himself the marks of enjoyment with another beloved,
Krishna came into this kunja.

Glancing in great anger at the brazen nayaka,
Radha here is in the state of the khandita-nayika.

There:
She to whom her lover, having let the agreed time pass, having enjoyed another,
marked with the signs of enjoyment, comes [only] in the morning — she indeed is khandita.
She is given to anger, sighs, silence and the like.

Rai in the tamala kunja is in the state of vipralabdha:
Krishna was to come — and has not come, She ponders in Her heart.

This is that very tamala kunja — see, Srinivasa,
how the actions of the vipralabdha are displayed everywhere.

There:
When, a tryst having been appointed, by fate the beloved [dear to her as] life does not come,
she whose heart is tormented is called by the wise vipralabdha;
[she] is given to despondency, anxious thoughts, sorrow, tears, swooning, sighs and the like.

Rai in this kunja is in the state of kalahantarita:
when the mana has passed, She is tormented here by remorse.

Her actions — incoherent speech and the rest — cannot be told;
seeing [this], the sakhis consider various means.

There:
She who before the sakhis in anger repulses her beloved who has come and fallen [at her feet],
and afterwards is tormented — she indeed is kalahantarita.
Her [actions] are incoherent speech, burning anguish, exhaustion, sighs and the like.*
notes: "Fallen [at her feet]" follows the 1960 edition (its Bengali rendering of the verse has পদানত); the text has prāptaṁ patitaṁ, "who has come [and] fallen".

verses_en.text:
Radhika here is in the state of proshita-bhartrika:
when Krishna goes to a distant land, She cannot find rest.

There:
When Krishna goes to a distant land, [the heroine] becomes proshita-bhartrika.*
Her [actions] are glorifying the beloved, dejection, thinness and sleeplessness,
untidiness, restlessness, numbness, anxious thoughts and the like — so it is held.
notes: "Krishna" follows the 1912/13 edition (by the scan of A: «দূরদেশং গতে কৃষ্ণে»); the 1960 edition has কান্তে, "the beloved".

verses_en.text:
When Akrura, taking Krishna, was setting out for Mathura,
what Rai became here cannot be told.

Thus [it is said] in the poem Hamsa-duta, the second verse:
When Mukunda, the Madana of the gopis' hearts, from the house of Nanda
set out for Madhupuri, following the son of Gandini,
then Radha, suffering in separation, whirling in dense eddies, sank
into the fathomless river of anxiety whose waters are torment.*
notes: The son of Gandini is Akrura (see 3601). The Hamsa-duta is a poem by Sri Rupa Gosvami.

verses_en.text:
What shall I say? Akrura has no fame in Vraja:
even today, in pain, they call Akrura "krura."*
notes: A play on words: the name Akrura means "not cruel," krura means "cruel."

verses_en.text:
[All] censure Akrura to one another again and again:
he does not understand what the inmost heart of Vraja is like.

To Gandini, his own mother, at the time of his birth
he gave great suffering — he, her son.

No one can bear to hear Akrura's name;
merely remembering [him], they swim in an ocean of grief.

Look: on the bank of the Yamuna is a kunja full of beauty;
here Rai and Kanu — with what bliss They sport!

Whatever Rai says to Krishna at the end of love's play,
that very thing Krishna does, wholly subject to prema.

Radha manifests the state of svadhina-bhartrika;
the wondrous delights [here] at every moment cannot be told.*
notes: Svadhina-bhartrika, "she whose husband is under [her] sway": one of the eight states of the heroine (nayika) in the Ujjvala-nilamani; the definition is in 3606.

verses_en.text:
Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, in [the section on] the kinds of heroines, the forty-ninth definition:
She whose beloved is near and under her sway is svadhina-bhartrika;
she engages in play in the water and in the forest, gathers flowers and so on.

O Srinivasa! In this flower grove
Radha and Madhava wander, surrounded by the sakhis.

In anuraga Radhika's heart overflows;
[one of] the actions of anuraga — the state of prema-vaichittya is attained.

In the same place, in [the section on] sthayi-bhava, the hundred and twelfth definition:
The raga that makes the beloved, though constantly experienced, ever new and new,
and itself becomes ever new and new, is called anuraga.*
notes: The number of the definition follows the 1912/13 edition (by the scan of A: «স্থায়িভাবপ্রকরণে ১১২ লক্ষণং»); the 1960 edition has the hundred and second.

verses_en.text:
Mutual subjugation, and likewise prema-vaichittya,
the greatest longing to be born even among insentient things,
in separation His appearing [before the eyes]: such are the actions here.

And how [it is]: in the state of prema-vaichittya, from excess of prema,
the thought of separation arises — and Radhika is distraught.

"Where is Krishna?" [She] says, and tears pour from Her eyes;
Krishna is right near — this She does not remember.

In the same place:
When even in the nearness of the beloved, by the very nature of the excellence of prema,
pain [arises] from the thought of separation, that is called prema-vaichittya.

Prema-vaichittya is not separate from sambhoga:
the [kinds] sampanna and samriddhiman are fully in accord with it.*
notes: Sambhoga is the enjoyment of union; in the Ujjvala-nilamani it is of four kinds: sankshipta ("brief"), sankirna ("mixed"), sampanna ("full") and samriddhiman ("perfect"). The same work counts prema-vaichittya among the kinds of separation (vipralambha); Narahari stresses that it is felt in the very midst of union.

verses_en.text:
The play of prema-vaichittya is supremely sweet;
poets describe it, and by this suffering goes far away.

As [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
Rai and Kanu, in the rapture of rasa,
sit on one seat, and the sakhis on all four sides.

What waves of anuraga!
The fair one cannot keep Her composure; Her body has grown weak.

Again and again [She] asks a sakhi:
"Where has the lord of my life gone, leaving me?

Shall I ever find the lord of my life again?" —
saying this, She strikes Her own head with Her hand.

[She] is drowned in the tears of both eyes;
heaving long sighs, She rolls on the ground.

The crown of rasikas, Shyama-raya,
seeing [Her] grave condition, consoles Radha.

The consolation refreshed [Her] life;
the thought of separation vanished, sorrow went far away.

What did the sakhi say with the corner of her eye?
Thrilled with rapture, [They] sport in secret.

Kala embraces [Her], opening His arms;
in shyness Rai, Her face lowered, smiles softly, softly.

Madhava cannot hold back His composure:
intoxicated with the wine of Madana, He presses His face to [Her] face.

As soon as [He] touches the high breasts with His hand,
[She] knows not where She is: how much rises in the heart!

Smiling, [He] loosens the knot of [Her] waistband;
[They] remain on the bed of flowers, stretched out.*
notes: কুসুম-শেষে (kusuma-śeṣe) in all copies; understood as কুসুম-শেজে, "on the bed of flowers"; so also in A by the scan («রহয়ে কুসুমশেষে অঙ্গ গড়াইয়া»).

verses_en.text:
Body mingled with body, They shine thus,
like a blue sapphire and gold, like lightning and a cloud.

The merriment grows beyond measure:
having set each other's attire in order, the two gaze [at each other].

Knowing the [right] time, a companion,
to ease [Their] weariness, speaks of many things softly, softly.

Narahari, at the sakhi's sign,
makes a fresh breeze to dispel the sweat.

O Srinivasa! In this grove by the Kalindi
Krishna sports with friends of five kinds.

Cheta, vita, vidushaka, pithamarda,
and also priya-narma — these five are His helpers.*
notes: The helpers (sahaya) of the hero according to the Ujjvala-nilamani: the cheta, a clever servant who arranges meetings; the vita, an expert in attire and in the science of love; the vidushaka, a jester fond of food; the pithamarda, a friend almost equal to the hero; the priya-narma-sakha, an intimate friend initiated into the deepest secrets (the definitions are in 3635–3646).

verses_en.text:
In various ways they help Krishna;
who does not sing the virtues of all these friends?

Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, in [the section on] the kinds of helpers, the first definition:
Now, His helpers are of five kinds: the chetaka, the vita,
the vidushaka, the pithamarda, and likewise the priya-narma-sakha.
Skill in jesting, ever-deep attachment,

knowledge of place and time, adroitness, the power to appease angry gopis,
the keeping of secret counsel and the like — these are held to be the virtues of the helpers.

Here Krishna with the chetas — Bhringa, Bhangura and others —
sports; all of them are skilled in every kind of contrivance.

Thus [it is said] in the same place:
The cheta is clever at arranging [meetings], secret in his deeds, bold of mind;
here in Gokula he is said to be Bhangura, Bhringara and others.*
notes: In the Bengali couplet 3637 the name is Bhringa; in the verse, Bhringara.

verses_en.text:
Here too are the vita friends — Kadara, Bharati and others,
skilled in adorning Krishna: wondrous is [their] way.*
notes: In the verse 3640 the name is Bharatibandha.

verses_en.text:
In the same place:
Skilled in attire and adornment, cunning, expert in gatherings,
knowing the arts of the science of love — he is called a vita;
Kadara, Bharatibandha and the rest are declared vitas.

Here the vidushaka friends — Vasanta and others —
increase the merriment while Krishna eats.

In the same place:
Named Vasanta and so on, greedy for food, fond of quarrels,
causing laughter by grotesque gestures, speech and dress — [such is] the vidushaka;
as this Madhumangala, famed in the Vidagdha-madhava.

The pithamarda Shridama — there is no end to his virtues;
how much he helps Krishna here!

In the same place:
He who in virtues is like the hero (nayaka) and follows him with love
is called a pithamarda; such is Shridama to Hari.

Here are the priya-narma-sakhas — Subala and others:
whatever brings Krishna happiness, that they do in every way.

In the same place:
Knowing the most intimate secrets, having taken up the mood of a sakhi,
he, the best of all loving friends, is the priya-narma-sakha;
in Gokula he is Subala, and likewise Arjuna and others.*
notes: Arjuna is a cowherd boy, an intimate friend of Krishna in Vraja (not the son of Pandu).

verses_en.text:
O Srinivasa! In this charming grove Krishna
Himself meets [the gopis]: with the sound of the flute He draws the gopis.

Just as Radhika has a svayam-duti and apta-dutis,
so too does Sri Krishna: in this is boundless bliss.*
notes: Svayam-duti, "one's own messenger": a lover who reveals his or her love in person; apta-duti, "a trusted messenger" (see 3649–3653, 3670–3673).

verses_en.text:
In the same place:
The messengers who will be described in the section on Hari's beloveds —
here too they should be understood by the knowers of rasa as is fitting.
There — svayam (Himself) and vamshi (the flute). ("Svayam" means svayam-duti.)

Vira, Vrinda and others are Sri Krishna's apta-dutis;
in this kunja they bring the two [of Them] together — what a wondrous way!

In the same place:
Vira, Vrinda and others are also celebrated as Krishna's trusted messengers:
Vira is bold of speech, Vrinda skilled in flattering words.

Vira and the rest are said to be Hari's own special messengers;
but those who will be described, ending with Lingini, are common to both.*
notes: Translated after the 1960 edition, অস্যাসাধারণা (asyāsādhāraṇāḥ, "His special"); A by the scan has «অন্যাঃ সাধারণা দূত্যো» ("other — common messengers"), C অস্যাঃ সাধারণা; the reading of the 1960 edition is adopted, as it agrees with the second line (where those "common to both" are contrasted with the special ones). Lingini is a wandering female ascetic, one of the messengers in the Ujjvala-nilamani.

verses_en.text:
What shall I say of how here Radhika's sakhis and the others
help [Her]? This cannot be told in detail.

Radhika's sakhis are of five kinds: sakhis, and further
nitya-sakhis, prana-sakhis and the rest — so [it is] known.

Taking all these sakhis, the beautiful Radhika
stays in this kunja, watching the path of Krishna.

In the same place:
The sakhis of the Queen of Vrindavana are held to be of five kinds:
sakhis, and nitya-sakhis, and certain prana-sakhis,
and priya-sakhis, and the renowned parama-preshtha-sakhis.

The sakhis Kusumika, Vindhya, Dhanishtha and others here
diligently fulfill what is in Radhika's heart.

In the same place:
The sakhis are celebrated as Kusumika, Vindhya, Dhanishtha and others.

The nitya-sakhis — Kasturi, Manimanjarika and others —
here ceaselessly fulfill Radha's wishes.

In the same place:
And the nitya-sakhis are Kasturi, Manimanjarika and others.

The prana-sakhis — Vasanti and others — are almost equal to Radha;
in this kunja they increase the merriment of Radha and Krishna.

In the same place:
The prana-sakhis are Shashimukhi, Vasanti, Lasika and others;
they have for the most part attained likeness (svarupata) to the Queen of Vrindavana.
("Svarupata" means equality.)*
notes: The gloss follows the 1912/13 edition (B); it is absent from the 1960 edition.

verses_en.text:
The priya-sakhis — Kurangakshi and others, incomparable —
in this kunja, seeing the beauty of the two [of Them], are overwhelmed.

In the same place:
The priya-sakhis are Kurangakshi, Sumadhya, Madanalasa,
Kamala, Madhuri, Manjukeshi, Kandarpa-sundari,
Madhavi, Malati, Kamalata, Shashikala and others.

The parama-preshtha-sakhis — Lalita and others — here,
having brought the two [of Them] together, are full of great joy at heart.

In the same place:
And the parama-preshtha-sakhis are Lalita together with Vishakhika,
Suchitra, Champakalata, Tungavidya, Indulekhika,

Rangadevi and Sudevi — these eight are foremost of all the groups;*
among them, in two alone, by the supreme height of prema,
here and there at times, here and there at times, a pre-eminence is, as it were, seen.
notes: সর্বগণাগ্রিমাঃ in A (checked against the scan)/B, "foremost of all the groups"; C and the 1960 edition have সর্বগুণাগ্রিমাঃ, "foremost in all virtues."

verses_en.text:
O Srinivasa! In this nikunja abode
the svayam-duti and the apta-dutis display [their] cleverness.

Thus [it is said] in the same place:
Now, of these who have recourse to helpers out of thirst for union with Krishna,
the way [they] employ messengers in purva-raga and the rest is described;
the messenger here is declared to be of two kinds: herself (svayam) and trusted (apta).

The svayam-duti here, seeing Krishna,
achieves her aim — by word, by body and by glance.

The svayam-duti Sri Radhika is skilled in every respect;
[She] sports in this kunja — there is no limit to the happiness.

In the same place:
She whose shyness breaks down from excessive eagerness and who, bewitched by raga and the like,
herself declares [her love] — she is therefore known as svayam-duti.
[Her] own declarations are said to be of three kinds: verbal, bodily and visual.

O Srinivasa! In this kadamba grove
the apta-dutis always desire Radha's happiness.

The doings of the trusted messengers cannot be told;
they are three: amitartha, nisrishtartha, patrahari.*
notes: The kinds of trusted messengers (apta-duti) according to the Ujjvala-nilamani: the amitartha guesses [the feelings of both] from hints on her own, the nisrishtartha is the one entrusted with the task, the patrahari carries letters (3677–3682).

verses_en.text:
In the same [work]:
She who would not break trust even at the cost of life,
affectionate and eloquent — she is the messenger of the fair-browed gopis;
she is of three kinds: amitartha, nisrishtartha and patrahari.
(Vishrambha means trust.)

The amitartha messenger, highly skilled in [reading] hints,
devising a means, unites the two here.

In the same [work]:
She who, knowing from signs the feeling of both or of one of the two,
unites the two by [various] means — she is the amitartha.

To the nisrishtartha messenger the burden of the task is entrusted;
in this kunja she arranges the meeting of the two by stratagem.

In the same [work]:
She to whom one of the two has entrusted the burden of the task,
and who brings both together by stratagem — she is called the nisrishtartha.

The patrahari messenger merely takes a letter
and gives [it] to the two, and the two meet, coming to the nikunja.

In the same [work]:
She who only carries messages for the young pair is the patraharika.

The messengers — the craftswoman, the astrologer, the ascetic, and also
the maidservant, the foster-sister — are known everywhere;*
notes: The craftswoman (shilpakari), the astrologer (daivajna), the ascetic (lingini), the maidservant (paricharika), the foster-sister (dhatreyi, the daughter of a nurse), the forest goddesses (vana-devi) and the sakhi are the kinds of messengers in the Ujjvala-nilamani (3685).

verses_en.text:
the forest goddesses, the sakhi and others — all of them in these kunjas
with joyful hearts reveal each her own qualities.

Thus [it is said] in the same [work]:
They are the craftswoman, the astrologer, the ascetic, the maidservant,
the foster-sister, the forest goddess, the sakhi and others — in Vraja.

The craftswoman, versed here in many crafts,
showing [her] craft, delights the two.

The trusted messenger who is an astrologer, expert in calculation,
foretells the meeting of the two in this kunja today.*
notes: "Today" follows A (by the scan: «কহে এই কুঞ্জে অদ্য দোঁহার ঘটনা») and B (অদ্য, adya); the 1960 edition has অন্য (anya, "another").

verses_en.text:
The ascetic is one in the dress of a female ascetic, like Paurnamasi;
Paurnamasi, coming here, unites the two.

In the same [work]:
The ascetic, in the dress of a female ascetic, is described as like Paurnamasi.

The maidservants, Lavanga Manjari and others, joyfully
unite Radhika with Krishna in this kunja.*
notes: Lavanga Manjari and Bhanumati are Radha's maidservants (paricharikas).

verses_en.text:
In the same [work]:
Lavanga Manjari, Bhanumati and others are the maidservants.

The foster-sister, bringing Radha from Javata,
playfully unites Her with Krishna in this kunja.

The forest goddesses stay in the forest at all times;
in this kunja they see the meeting of Rai and Kanu.

The sakhi playfully unites the two in this kunja;
the way of the sakhi is well known — who does not sing [her] glory?

In the same [work]:
She who guilelessly bears a mutual prema greater even than for herself,
trusting, alike in age, dress and the like, is considered a sakhi.

Her service as messenger to both is twofold: explicit and suggested.
(Tat means of this sakhi; ubhayoh means of the hero and the heroine.)

In various ways, in this nikunja abode,
the sakhi expands the happiness of the two in sambhoga.*
notes: Sambhoga is the enjoyment of the lovers' union, as opposed to vipralambha (separation). Primary (mukhya) sambhoga is in waking life, secondary (gauna) in dreams; each is of four kinds (3698–3701).

verses_en.text:
As primary and secondary, sambhoga is of eight kinds:
after purva-raga and the rest, sankshipta and the rest — so it is set forth.

Thus [it is said] in the same [work]:
The feeling that, through the favourable enjoyment of seeing, embracing and the like,
rises to the exultation of the young pair is called sambhoga.

By the wise it is declared twofold: primary and secondary.
Primary sambhoga is in the waking state; it is of four kinds.

Those arising in order after purva-raga, after mana and after the two [kinds of] pravasa
they know as sankshipta, sankirna, sampanna and samriddhiman.*
notes: Pravasa is separation through the beloved's going away, either not far or far. Sankshipta means "brief", sankirna "mixed", sampanna "attained", samriddhiman "abundant" sambhoga (3702–3712).

verses_en.text:
In purva-raga there is sankshipta sambhoga: briefly
the sakhi unites the two here in her own way.

In the same [work]:
Where the young pair, out of fear, shyness and the like,
enjoy restrained caresses — that [sambhoga] is called sankshipta.

When the mana has been overcome in various ways,
here, in sankirna sambhoga, the sakhi finds happiness.

In the same [work]:
Where the caresses are mixed with the remembrance of offences and the like,
that [sambhoga] is sankirna, pleasing like slightly heated sugarcane.

After a pravasa not far away there is sampanna; it has two kinds;
here the sakhi tastes the happiness of sambhoga.

In the same [work]:
The enjoyment when the beloved has come together [with her] after pravasa is called sampanna;
that union is twofold: agati and pradurbhava.

Agati:
Arrival in accordance with worldly conduct is agati.

Pradurbhava:
When before His dearest ones, overwhelmed by the agitation of prema, Hari
suddenly appears — that is called pradurbhava.

Samriddhiman sambhoga comes after distant pravasa;
by the distinction of concealed and manifest it unfolds in this kunja.

In the same [work]:
The overflowing enjoyment of a young pair separated through dependence [on others],
for whom the sight of each other is hard to obtain, is called samriddhiman.

In the same [work]:
Some accept a twofold form of these, by the distinction of concealed and manifest;
though it is accepted, it is not stated here, since it does not produce great exultation.

O Srinivasa, by this path Rai joyfully
enters this kunja house together with Her companions.

However many companions Radhika has, there is no end to them;
among the sakhis headed by Lalita there is a wondrous beauty.

The sakhi Sri Lalita, perfect in all qualities,
is surrounded by her eight [companions], Ratnaprabha and the others.*
notes: All copies read অষ্টগুণে ("with eight qualities"); by sense and by 3717–3729 — অষ্টগণে ("with her eight companions").

verses_en.text:
Thus [it is said] in the Sri Brihat-krishna-ganoddesha-dipika:
Ratnaprabha, Ratikala, Subhadra, Bhadrarekhika,
Sumukhi, and Dhanishtha, and Kalahamsi, Kalapini.*
notes: The title follows A/B (শ্রীবৃহৎকৃষ্ণগণোদ্দেশদীপিকায়াং); it is garbled in the 1960 edition. Apparently the longer recension of Rupa Gosvami's Radha-krishna-ganoddesha-dipika. Verses 3716–3730 list the eight companions attached to each of Radha's eight principal sakhis.

verses_en.text:
Vishakha's beauty has no comparison;
surrounded by her eight [companions], Madhavi and the others, she shines.

Thus [it is said] in the same [work]:
Malati, Madhavi, Chandrarekhika, and also Kunjari,
Harini, [the one] named Chapala, Surabhi and Shubhanana.*
notes: The order "Malati, Madhavi" follows A/B/C; the 1960 edition names Madhavi first, as in 3717.

verses_en.text:
Skilled in everything, of excellent conduct, Suchitra*
is accompanied by her own eight, Kurangakshi and the others.
notes: All copies read সুচিত্রাদি (suchitrādi, "Suchitra and the others"); translated by sense.

verses_en.text:
In the same [work]:
Kurangakshi, Sucharita, Mandali, Manikundala,
Chandrika, Chandralatika, Kundakakshi, Sumandira.

Champakalata's sweetness is wondrous beyond measure;
with her eight [companions], Rasalika and the others, the beauty is a marvel.

In the same [work]:
Rasalika, Tilakini, Shauraseni, Sugandhika,
Kamini, Kamanagari, Nagari, Nagavenika.*
notes: Kamini follows A (by the scan: «কামিনী কামনগরী») and B; the 1960 edition has রামিনী (Ramini), C বামিনী (Vamini).

verses_en.text:
Who can keep composure at [the sight of] Sri Rangadevi's beauty?
The beauty of her eight, Manjumedha and the others, steals the heart.

In the same [work]:
Manjumedha, Sumadhura, Sumadhya, Madhurekshana,
Tanumadhya, Madhusandra, Gunachuda, Varangada.

Sudevi is always blossoming with love for Radhika;
her eight, Tungabhadra and the others, are well known.

In the same [work]:
Tungabhadra, Rasottunga, Rangavati, Susangata,
Chitralekha, Vichitrangi, Medini, Madanalasa.*
notes: Rangavati follows A (by the scan: «রঙ্গবাটী সুসঙ্গতা»), B and C; the 1960 edition has রঙ্গবাটা (Rangavata).

verses_en.text:
Tungavidya is a supreme beauty, her loveliness is great;
her eight, Kalakanthi and the others, are of wondrous ways.

In the same [work]:
Kalakanthi, Shashikala, Kamala, Madhura, Indira,
Kandarpasundari, Kamalatika, Premamanjari.*
notes: মধুরেন্দিরা is taken as two names, Madhura and Indira; otherwise the list has seven names.

verses_en.text:
Indulekha is of excellent conduct and attracts all hearts;
to what can her eight, Kaveri and the others, be compared?

In the same [work]:
Kaveri, Charukavara, Sukeshi, Manjukeshika,
Harahira, Mahahira, Harakanthi, Manohara.

O Srinivasa, together with the companions of Lalita and the others,
in this kunja, joyfully seeing the meeting of the two,

moment by moment [they] cannot contain their hearts for exultation —
[such] are the supremely wondrous deeds of the sakhis, Lalita and the others.

Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani:
Mutual praise of the love (1) and the qualities (2) [of both], awakening attachment in them (3),
[arranging] the abhisara (4) for the two of them, giving a sakhi to Krishna (5),
jests (6), consolation (7), dressing (8), skill in revealing [the feelings of] the heart (9),
hiding her faults (10), deceiving the husband and others (11),*
notes: Ujjvala-nilamani, the section on sakhis: the seventeen activities of a sakhi. The numbers (1)–(17) are in the text of the 1888 and 1912/13 editions; the 1960 edition does not have them.

verses_en.text:
instruction (12), bringing [them] together at the right time (13), service with the fan and the like (14),
reproaches to both of them (15), and also sending messages (16),
efforts and the like to preserve the heroine's life (17) — [these] are the activities of a sakhi.
O Srinivasa, there are no words to describe it:

anuragavalli.title: Прощальный обход Враджа Шринивасой и Нароттамой
anuragavalli.summary: С провожатым от Дживы они обходят Мадхувану, Талавану, Кумудавану, Бахулавану, Радха-кунду (у Рагхунатхи Даса), Говардхану, Ади-Бадри, Камьявану, Варшану, Нандаграм, Кхадиравану, Яват, Кокила-вану, Шеша-шаи, Бхандиравану, Раваль, Гокулу и Матхуру.

verses.text:
Утром встав, оба совершили омовение и прочее
и простились с Госани во всех местах.

Шри Джива Госани дал им в спутники
одного сведущего вайшнава, чтобы показывать все места.

Вечером они остановились в Шри Мадхупури;
наутро омывшись в Мадхуване,

увидев там Талавану и Кумудавану,
провели ту ночь с радостью в сердце.

На рассвете, повидав Бахулавану,
придя к Радха-кунде, совершили омовение и прочее.

Распростёршись в поклоне перед Шри Дасом Госани,
они там и отдыхали ночью.

По порядку всю историю Госани
рассказали; слушая, Госани радовался в сердце.

В беседах о Кришне (ночь) прошла словно миг;
утром встав, они совершили омовение и памятование.
[с. 81]

Обойдя Шри Кунду по правую руку, Говардхану
пошли обходить они, с переполненным сердцем.

Всегда на устах имена: Радха, Кришна, Говинда;
видя места лил и служение — какое блаженство!

Слёзы, трепет, дрожь восторга и прочие преображения бхавы —
сколько мне писать? Очень уж это пространно.

Вкушая тайну каждого места, оба
падают на землю, погружённые (в бхаву).

Через некоторое время, придя в себя, снова бегут,
идут к другому месту лил и получают даршан.

В одном месте я написал, лишь указав направление;
знайте, что повсюду было так же.

Обойдя Говардхану, они вернулись
и ту ночь провели у стоп Даса Госани.

Всевозможно явил им Госани милость —
кто есть такой, кто это опишет?

Как плакали при прощании —
рассказывая ту скорбь, испытываю великую муку.

Оттуда, идя и идя, они пришли в Парамандалу*
и, увидев Ади-Бадри, поклонились.
notes: «Парамандала» — так в издании; видимо, селение во Врадже близ Ади-Бадри.

verses.text:
Проведя там ночь, утром пошли в Камьявану
и повсюду видели места по порядку.

Оттуда пришли в Вришабханупур;
глядя на всё, из глаз текут потоки слёз.
[с. 82]

Тогда там не было ни служения, ни храма —
потому я о нём и не написал.

Проведя ту ночь, увидев Према-саровару,
они обрадовались даршану Санкеты.

Проведя там ту ночь, пошли в Нандаграм,
увидели царя Враджа с его спутниками и поклонились.

В Павана-сароваре совершили омовение и прочее;
какое поднялось блаженство — не высказать.

Вокруг они видели места лил;
утром, идя и идя, пришли в Кхадиравану.

Оттуда пошли в селение по имени Яват;
увидев места лил, там отдохнули.

Утром, когда увидели Кокила-вану, —
какое было блаженство, не могу сказать.

Увидев Батхаин, видят Чарана-пахари;
видя следы стоп и прочее, весьма обрадовались.

Спутник показывает с горы
все селения, какие есть вокруг.

Увидев там тайну (лилы), пошли в Дахи-гаон;
ту ночь, в счастливых беседах о Кришне, там и провели.

Утром, идя в селение Котимани,
обрели блаженство, видя рощу кадамб.

Оттуда, идя и идя, пришли к Шеша-шаи;
в кунде по имени Кшира-самудра омылись и совершили памятование.
[с. 83]

Получили даршан Шри Лакшми-Нараяны
и ту ночь также провели там.

Игру Шеша-шаи совершает сын царя Враджа —
рассказывая об этом, оба вкушали счастье.

Оттуда пришли в селение Кхайра;
увидев Санджхои, там отдохнули.

Затем, повидав Уджани,
пошли отдохнуть в Кхелана-вану.

Затем Рамагхат, Акшая-ват,
Гопигхат увидели они у Ямуны.

В тот день, придя в Чира-гхат, остались там;
на следующее утро пришли к Нанда-гхату.

Совершив омовение и прочее, радостно пошли;
переправившись через Шри Ямуну, пришли в Бхадравану.

Затем, совершив омовение в Бхандираване,
пришли в Белавану, весьма погружённые в прему.

Видя лес на берегу Ямуны, обрадовались;
видя на том берегу красоту Вриндавана, изумились.

Тот день они провели там в радости даршана;
на следующий день отдыхали в Лохаване.

Манаса-саровара находится в пределах Вриндавана;
Ямуна течёт к северу от этого озера —

потому в описании обхода я его не упомянул.
Утром пошли они по берегу Ямуны.
[с. 84]

Идя и идя, дойдя до селения Раваль,
увидев место рождения Шри Радхики, —

какое было блаженство, того не вместить телу;
там и остались — от премы не могут идти.

Затем отправились в Гокулу;
увидев красоту, отдохнули в Махаване.

Там, увидев дом Нанды и разные места лил, —
какое было счастье, тому свидетели лишь они.
Затем в Матхуре, в Вишранти — полдень;

verses_en.text:
Rising in the morning, both bathed and so on
and took leave of the Gosanis everywhere.

Sri Jiva Gosani gave them as companion
a knowledgeable Vaishnava to show them all the places.

In the evening they stopped at Sri Madhupuri;
the next morning, having bathed at Madhuvana,

having seen Talavana and Kumudavana there,
they spent that night with joyful hearts.

At dawn, having seen Bahulavana,
coming to Radha-kunda they bathed and so on.

Offering dandavat obeisances to Sri Dasa Gosani,
they rested there that night.

In order they told Gosani
the whole story; hearing it, Gosani rejoiced at heart.

In talk of Krishna (the night) passed like a moment;
rising in the morning, they bathed and performed remembrance.
[p. 81]

Keeping Sri Kunda on their right, Govardhana
they set out to circumambulate, their hearts overflowing.

The names always on their lips: Radha, Krishna, Govinda;
seeing the places of the pastimes and the service — what bliss!

Tears, trembling, thrills and other transformations of bhava —
how much shall I write? It is far too extensive.

Relishing the secret of each place, both
fall to the ground, absorbed (in bhava).

After a while, regaining awareness, they hurry on again,
go to another place of the pastimes and receive darshana.

In one place I have written, merely pointing the direction;
know that everywhere it was the same.

Having circumambulated Govardhana, they returned
and spent that night at the feet of Dasa Gosani.

In many ways Gosani showed them mercy —
who is there who could describe it?

How they wept at parting —
telling of that sorrow, I feel great anguish.

From there, walking on and on, they came to Paramandala*
and, seeing Adi-Badri, bowed down.
notes: "Paramandala" — so in the edition; apparently a village in Vraja near Adi-Badri.

verses_en.text:
Spending the night there, in the morning they went to Kamyavana
and saw all the places in order.

From there they came to Vrishabhanupura;
looking at everything, streams of tears flow from their eyes.
[p. 82]

At that time there was neither service nor temple there —
therefore I have not written about it.

Spending that night and seeing Prema-sarovara,
they rejoiced at the darshana of Sanketa.

Spending that night there, they went to Nandagrama,
saw the king of Vraja with his associates and bowed down.

In Pavana-sarovara they bathed and so on;
the bliss that arose cannot be told.

All around they saw the places of the pastimes;
in the morning, walking on, they came to Khadiravana.

From there they went to the village called Yavat;
seeing the places of the pastimes, they rested there.

In the morning, when they saw Kokila-vana —
the bliss that came I cannot describe.

Having seen Bathain, they see Charana-pahari;
seeing the footprints and other marks, they were very glad.

Their companion shows them from the hill
all the villages there are around.

Having seen the secret (of the pastime) there, they went to Dahi-gaon;
that night, in happy talk of Krishna, they spent there.

In the morning, going to the village of Kotimani,
they found bliss in seeing the kadamba grove.

From there, walking on, they came to Shesha-shayi;
in the kunda called Kshira-samudra they bathed and performed remembrance.
[p. 83]

They received the darshana of Sri Lakshmi-Narayana
and spent that night there as well.

The son of the king of Vraja performs the Shesha-shayi pastime —
telling of this, both relished happiness.

From there they came to the village of Khayra;
having seen Sanjhoi, they rested there.

Then, having seen Ujani,
they went to rest at Khelana-vana.

Then Ramaghat, Akshaya-vata,
Gopighat they saw near the Yamuna.

That day, coming to Chira-ghat, they stayed there;
the next morning they arrived at Nanda-ghat.

Having bathed and so on, they went on joyfully;
crossing the Sri Yamuna, they went to Bhadravana.

Then, having bathed at Bhandiravana,
they went to Belavana, deeply absorbed in prema.

Seeing the forest on the Yamuna's bank, they rejoiced;
seeing the beauty of Vrindavana on the far bank, they were amazed.

That day they stayed there in the joy of darshana;
the next day they rested at Lohavana.

Manasa-sarovara lies within Vrindavana;
the Yamuna flows to the north of that lake —

therefore I have not mentioned it in the account of the circuit.
In the morning they took the road along the Yamuna.
[p. 84]

Walking on and on, reaching the village of Raval,
seeing the birthplace of Sri Radhika —

the bliss that came could not be contained in their bodies;
they stayed right there — for prema they could not walk.

Then they set out for Gokula;
seeing its beauty, they rested at Mahavana.

There, seeing Nanda's house and the various places of the pastimes —
what happiness they felt, only they are witness.
Then at Mathura, at Vishranti — midday;
